extracted.intended_audience: emerging African writers applying to the Caine Prize Online Editing Programme
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for applying to the Caine Prize 12-week Online Editing Programme: eligibility, permitted genres, required submission materials, and rights/contract terms for selected participants. Targets emerging African short-story writers seeking developmental editing and publication in the Caine Prize anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme scope and offer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Online Editing Programme is a tailored, 12-week initiative focusing on fiction writing. It provides structured support to selected emerging African writers through one-to-one guidance, group workshops and written feedback enabling writers to develop new short stories from draft to publishable standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to developmental editing support, participants gain industry insight and networking through interactive Q&A sessions and masterclasses led by influential contemporary literary figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Be 18 years or older at the time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: African writer definition / nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Be an African writer - this is taken to mean someone who was born in Africa, or who is a national of an African country, or who has a parent who is African by birth or nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Caine Prize reserves the right to request proof of nationality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme is open to emerging African writers residing either on the continent or in the diaspora.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both Africa-based and diaspora African writers are eligible if they meet other criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication history requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Have at least two short stories published in established print or online outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-published work does not qualify; applicants must provide at least two proofs of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: No full-length book or short story collection published
rubrics_metrics.description: Have not published a full-length book (fiction or non-fiction) or short story collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This opportunity targets emerging writers without book-length publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No major award wins/shortlistings
rubrics_metrics.description: Have not won or been shortlisted for any national, regional, or international literary award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past recognition at those levels disqualifies applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible genre — fiction short stories only
rubrics_metrics.description: This opportunity is specifically for African writers working on short stories. Only fictional short stories will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following genres are not eligible: novels; children’s literature; non-fiction (including journalism, essays, memoirs, biographies, etc.); academic writing; drama or plays; poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story summary length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A story summary (no more than 300 words) outlining the short story they wish to develop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries must be concise and stay within the 300-word limit requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bio length and content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief bio (no more than 150 words) that highlights relevant writing experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the bio under 150 words and focus on experience relevant to the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs of publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At least two proofs of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs must be for short stories published in established print or online outlets; self-published pieces do not count as qualifying proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-entry limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant may submit only one entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple entries from the same writer will lead to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must clearly state the writer’s African country of origin and the title or working title of the proposed short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of country of origin or title may render the submission ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and rights agreement for selected participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected participants must agree to have their completed stories published in the Caine Prize anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By participating, writers grant the Caine Prize exclusive global print and digital rights, effective from the date of contract signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility enforcement and non-compliant submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that submissions that do not meet these criteria will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Caine Prize may request proof of nationality and will disqualify submissions that fail to meet stated requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for queries
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any questions regarding eligibility or the submission process, contact info@caineprize.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers are available to assist with eligibility or submission questions prior to applying.
